source: CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) Recommended Child, Adolescent, and Adult Immunization Schedules

140.display: Influenza, split virus, trivalent, preservative free
140.plain_purpose: Annual seasonal flu vaccine to prevent influenza infection and severe respiratory complications.
140.series_rule: 1 dose annually each influenza season; doses recorded within 14 days across different sources (e.g., clinic EHR vs. state immunization registry) represent likely cross-source duplicate entries rather than separate clinical vaccinations.

141.plain_purpose: Annual seasonal flu vaccine to prevent influenza infection and complications.
141.series_rule: 1 dose annually each influenza season; doses recorded within 14 days across sources indicate a likely registry duplicate.

88.series_rule: 1 dose annually each influenza season; doses within 14 days indicate a likely duplicate record.

115.display: Tdap (Tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis vaccine, adsorbed)
115.plain_purpose: Protects adolescents and adults against tetanus (lockjaw), diphtheria, and pertussis (whooping cough).
115.series_rule: 1 adolescent booster dose at age 11–12 years, followed by a Td or Tdap booster every 10 years.

113.display: Td (adult), 5 Lf tetanus toxoid, preservative free, adsorbed
113.plain_purpose: Decennial adult booster vaccine protecting against tetanus and diphtheria.
113.series_rule: 1 booster dose every 10 years after initial Tdap series.

62.plain_purpose: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine protecting against HPV-related cancers.
62.series_rule: CDC ACIP recommends a 2-dose HPV schedule (0, 6–12 months) when initiated before age 15 (ages 9–14 years). A 3-dose schedule (0, 1–2, 6 months) is indicated only if initiated at age 15 years or older or in immunocompromised patients. A 3rd dose administered to a healthy adolescent who initiated the series before age 15 is an ACIP schedule over-immunization anomaly.

165.plain_purpose: 9-valent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine protecting against HPV-associated cancers.
165.series_rule: 2-dose schedule when initiated before age 15; 3-dose schedule when initiated at age 15 or older.

114.display: Meningococcal polysaccharide (Groups A, C, Y and W-135) diphtheria toxoid conjugate vaccine (MCV4P)
114.plain_purpose: MenACWY conjugate vaccine protecting against meningococcal meningitis and bloodstream infection.
114.series_rule: 2-dose adolescent series: primary dose at age 11–12 years with a booster dose at age 16 years.

208.display: COVID-19, mRNA, LNP-S, PF, 30 mcg/0.3 mL dose
208.plain_purpose: mRNA COVID-19 vaccine protecting against severe SARS-CoV-2 illness and hospitalization.
208.series_rule: Primary mRNA series doses are separated by at least 21 days (Pfizer-BioNTech) or 28 days (Moderna). Doses recorded within 14 days of each other across a clinic EHR and a retail pharmacy/state IIS feed represent a cross-source duplicate record.

213.plain_purpose: COVID-19 vaccine protecting against severe SARS-CoV-2 disease.
213.series_rule: Doses recorded within 14 days across sources indicate a cross-source duplicate record.

121.plain_purpose: Live attenuated shingles (herpes zoster) vaccine (Zostavax), historically given to older adults.
121.series_rule: Live zoster vaccine (Zostavax, CVX 121) was licensed as a single-dose vaccine and was discontinued in the United States in November 2020 in favor of the 2-dose recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix, CVX 187, spaced 2–6 months apart). Recording 2 doses of live zoster vaccine (CVX 121) represents an ACIP schedule/coding anomaly.

187.plain_purpose: Recombinant adjuvanted shingles vaccine (Shingrix) for adults aged 50 years and older.
187.series_rule: 2-dose series separated by 2 to 6 months for adults aged 50 years and older.
